text: The two pie charts show the proportion of the workforce employed in four sectors of the economy in 1990 and 2020. The figures are shown as percentages of all employees.

Overall, the most striking change was the dramatic growth of the service sector, which came to dominate employment, while agriculture and manufacturing both lost a substantial share of the workforce. Construction, by contrast, remained small and almost unchanged.

In 1990, services already employed the largest group of workers, at 45%, although manufacturing was not far behind with 32%. Agriculture accounted for 18% and construction for just 5%. Together, agriculture and manufacturing employed half of all workers, at 50%.

By 2020, the share of service workers had risen by 28 percentage points to 73%, meaning that almost three-quarters of employees worked in this sector. Manufacturing fell by nearly half to 17%, and agriculture declined most sharply in relative terms, dropping from 18% to only 4%. Construction edged up by one point to 6%. In total, the combined share of agriculture and manufacturing dropped from 50% to 21%.
